demo.title: Can You Challenge a Research Finding?

subject_revision.revision_status: local working copy; source revision not pinned

subject.question: Can a bounded, reproducible shortfall case challenge a policy-equivalence claim?
subject.scope: Path A is a valid same-input policy comparison using a test-only identifier variant of the calibration economics; a 12-unit per-row difference is recomputed, while novelty is not established. Path B is the target lifecycle and has no retained qualifying fixture.

verification.command: See evidence/research/shortfall-challenge/replay-instructions.md; run the focused Clojure test command from the PRF repository root.
verification.purpose: Freshly recompute both allocator results and exercise the candidate gate, preserving its current policy-root mismatch as a failing qualification result.

limitations: The finite result challenges the proposition for this input only; it is not a general proof or a finding about a live protocol.
The comparison requests share available capital, rows, requests, caps, rounding and tie-break settings; only redistribution policy differs.
The candidate pins different policy roots from those recomputed by the current allocator, and its source revision is not pinned, so candidate validation does not pass.
Both computed allocator results pass their invariant checks.
Challenge 001 is not frozen, published or open; no reviewer acceptance or reward is represented.
The test inputs retain the calibration economics and change only the allocation identifier; identifier changes alone do not establish novelty or qualify for reward.
